text.p: Tropical Storm Josephine is moving into northwestern Florida at this time. Josephine has top winds near 65 mph and will weaken a little and become extratropical this period, but will still be a fairly strong storm as it moves northward just inland of the East Coast. Heavy rains associated with the storm will be the main threat, with up to and locally over 5 inches of rain. Flooding will result in some areas, especially in the higher elevations of Georgia northward through the Virginias. As of 11pm Monday EDT, Tropical Storm Warnings are up for the Florida coast from Apalachicola to Venice, and on the east coast of Florida from Cape Canaveral to Little River Inlet in South Carolina.

Tropical Storm Genevieve, centered about 650 miles southwest of the southern tip of Baja, is drifting very slowly northwest. Top winds are 45 mph and should remain near 45 mph throughout the day as the storm moves very slowly to the northwest. This system is a moderate threat only to shipping but does not threaten any land areas at this time.
There are no further statements at this time.
